Sequence Plot (heatmap, index, or distribution)

Source: R/sequence_plot.R, R/sequence_plot_mcml.R
sequence_plot.Rd

sequence_plot() draws categorical sequences: one row per sequence and one coloured cell per time point, or the share of sequences in each state at every time point. Three views share one call:

  • type = "heatmap" (default): a dense carpet in a single panel, rows ordered by sort or a dendrogram.

  • type = "index": the same layout with optional thin gaps between rows and no dendrogram, split into one panel per group (group, or the clusters of a clustering) on an ncol x nrow grid.

  • type = "distribution": the stacked state distribution over time, drawn by distribution_plot().

It reads wide sequences, event logs (with action), networks built from sequences, clusterings, mixture fits and tna models; periods gives one row per actor with the time axis split into days, weeks or another period. An mcml from build_mcml() gets a multichannel figure instead: a macro Summary panel and one panel per cluster (see the section Multichannel view of an mcml). That figure is drawn with ggplot2 and takes only type, trim, state_colors, na_color, main, time_label (or xlab) and the mcml options (normalize, na, panel, expand, combine, rest, rest_label); every other figure is drawn with base graphics.

The plot describes the sequences; it does not model them. The row order of a heatmap comes from sort and is a display choice, so blocks of similar rows are a reason to cluster the sequences with build_clusters(), not a clustering in themselves. trim changes only what is drawn, never the data.

Usage

sequence_plot(
  x,
  type = c("heatmap", "index", "distribution"),
  sort = c("lcs", "frequency", "start", "end", "hamming", "osa", "lv", "dl", "qgram",
    "cosine", "jaccard", "jw"),
  tree = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  periods = NULL,
  fill = c("stretch", "pad"),
  actor = NULL,
  action = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  order = NULL,
  scale = c("proportion", "count"),
  geom = c("area", "bar"),
  na = TRUE,
  normalize = FALSE,
  trim = NULL,
  panel = c("both", "summary", "channels"),
  expand = NULL,
  combine = NULL,
  rest = c("clusters", "pooled", "none"),
  rest_label = "Other states",
  trim_clusterwise = FALSE,
  row_gap = 0,
  dendrogram_width = 1.2,
  k = NULL,
  k_color = "white",
  k_line_width = 2.5,
  state_colors = NULL,
  na_color = "grey90",
  cell_border = NA,
  frame = FALSE,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  main = NULL,
  show_n = TRUE,
  time_label = "Time",
  xlab = NULL,
  y_label = NULL,
  ylab = NULL,
  tick = NULL,
  ncol = NULL,
  nrow = NULL,
  combined = TRUE,
  legend = NULL,
  legend_size = NULL,
  legend_title = NULL,
  legend_ncol = NULL,
  legend_border = NA,
  legend_bty = "n",
  cols = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'mcml_sequence_plot'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

The sequences to draw:

event log

A data frame with one row per action and action naming the action column (with actor, time and order as needed). It is converted with prepare(): one row per actor, or per actor-period with periods.

data frame or matrix

One row per sequence, one column per time point; for a data frame, cols names the position columns when they are not a numbered run.

netobject

A network built from sequences; its sequence data is drawn. A network without its sequence data (built from a matrix) raises an error, and a one-hot or association network raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

net_clustering

From build_clusters(): its sequences, with the cluster assignments as groups and its distance matrix as the heatmap's dendrogram.

netobject_group

From cluster_network() or build_network() on a clustering: the full sequences and assignments carried by the clustering, or, for a plain group split, the groups' sequences stacked and labelled by group.

net_mmm

From build_mmm(): its sequences (or, when the fit stores none, those of its first component model), with the hard assignments as groups.

tna

A tna model; its integer-coded sequences are decoded to their state labels.

mcml

From build_mcml(), built from sequences (an mcml built from a matrix carries none and raises an error). It gives the multichannel figure: one panel per cluster plus a macro Summary panel. type = "heatmap" and "index" draw the carpet (each channel's own states solid, the other clusters a faded wash); type = "distribution" draws the stacked distribution (add normalize = TRUE for a TraMineR-style seqdplot, where each time point sums to 1).

For the print() method: an mcml_sequence_plot.

type

The view: "heatmap" (default), "index" or "distribution".

sort

How rows are ordered, in the heatmap and within each panel of the index view. "lcs" (default) orders them by a Ward (ward.D2) hierarchical clustering of their longest-common-subsequence distances, and any other build_clusters() distance ("hamming", "osa", "lv", "dl", "qgram", "cosine", "jaccard", "jw") does the same with that distance. "frequency" clusters the rows by how often each state occurs in them. "start" sorts the rows alphabetically by their states from the first time point on, "end" from the last time point back; these two draw no dendrogram. A clustering input (a net_clustering, or a netobject_group from cluster_network()) orders the heatmap by a hierarchical clustering of its own distance matrix, using its linkage when it was clustered hierarchically and ward.D2 otherwise (for example with the default pam), unless tree is given.

tree

A hclust, dendrogram or agnes object that gives the row order of the heatmap and is drawn beside it; it overrides sort. It must have one leaf per row. Default NULL.

group

The groups to draw in separate panels, one value per sequence (nrow(x) values), for the index and distribution views; the heatmap ignores it. NULL (default) uses the cluster assignments of a net_clustering, net_mmm or netobject_group input, and draws one panel otherwise. With periods, group instead names a column of the event log (or of the network's metadata) that is constant within actor, such as a class or a condition: one panel per value, one row per actor, all panels on the same period axis. With an event log it works only together with periods; otherwise it raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

periods

The column that splits each actor's sequence into periods (days, weeks, ...): a column of the event log, or of the network's metadata. x must be an event log with actor and action, or a netobject built with actor and session = periods, so that each actor-period pair holds one sequence; anything else raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input. The plot then has one row per actor and the time axis is split into equal-width blocks, one per period. A Date column gives one block per calendar day and a whole-number column (a day or week counter) one block per number, from the first to the last, so a period in which nobody acted is an empty block; factor levels give their order (an unused level is an empty block); other columns are sorted. Ticks mark the period boundaries and each label sits under its block; tick thins the labels, and the x-axis label defaults to the column name. Heatmap and index views only (the distribution view raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input). trim then counts periods, not time points. Default NULL plots the sequences as they are.

fill

With periods, how an actor's steps fill a block. "stretch" (default) spreads them over the whole block, so one step fills it and three steps take a third each; the cell width differs between actors. "pad" gives every block as many fixed slots as the busiest actor-period and leaves unused slots as NA, so a slot is the same step position for every actor (minor ticks mark the slots when there are at most 60 in all). With periods, empty space is white unless na_color is given, so it is never confused with a state drawn in grey. Repeats of a state merge into one spell; cell_border = "white" (TraMineR's border) outlines each action so they show as separate, equal shares of the period. Setting fill without periods raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input; an mcml ignores it.

actor, action, time, order

For an event log: column names, as in build_network(). Giving action declares x an event log (one row per action); actor identifies who acted (one row per actor in the plot), and time and order put each actor's actions in order (otherwise row order is used). Without periods, a time column also splits an actor's actions into sessions at gaps over 15 minutes, as prepare() does; with periods it does not, so each actor-period is one sequence. actor, time or order without action, a column that is not in x, and a missing actor or period raise an error of class nestimate_bad_input. Default NULL each.

scale, geom, na

For the distribution view, passed to distribution_plot(): scale is "proportion" (default) or "count", geom is "area" (default) or "bar", and na = TRUE (default) draws missing cells as a band of their own. For an mcml distribution, na = FALSE drops the NA (ended) band and shows every time point as shares of the sequences still running there, so each panel stacks to 100 percent (cluster panels only with rest = "clusters" or "pooled"; a time point where no sequence is running stays empty).

normalize

For an mcml distribution only: TRUE normalises each time point to sum to 1 within its channel (the composition of TraMineR's seqdplot); FALSE (default) shows prevalence, capped with an NA band.

trim

A cut of the time axis (one number) or of the time axis and the rows (two numbers), to stop a few long sequences from stretching the plot and a few near-empty ones from padding it. It applies to all three views, the mcml multichannel figure included. Default NULL plots everything.

The first number cuts the time axis. A fraction in (0, 1) judges each time point on its own activity and keeps the busiest ones that together hold that share of the observed states, ties going to the earlier one; the rest are removed wherever they sit and the kept ones close up under their own labels. So trim = 0.9 removes the quiet time points holding the last tenth of the states, which is what a long tail consists of, and those with no data. A value >= 1 is an absolute cut (trim = 50 keeps the first 50 time points). With periods the unit is the period block: trim = 60 keeps the first 60 periods and a fraction judges each period by its actions.

The second number ends each row earlier and never removes a row, counted over the time points kept by the first: a value >= 1 keeps each row's first that many observed states (trim = c(60, 5)), a fraction its first share of them (trim = c(0.9, 0.9)). What is left stays in place; the row is white after that point. NA leaves an axis alone (trim = c(NA, 5)). Either way only the drawing changes, not the data.

panel

For an mcml distribution only: which panels to draw. "both" (default) stacks the macro Summary channel and the per-cluster channels on one figure, each with its own legend; "summary" draws the macro channel alone, keyed and coloured by cluster; "channels" draws the per-cluster channels alone, keyed and coloured by state. The macro channel is keyed by cluster and the rest by state, so a cluster and a state can land on the same colour; drawing one panel avoids that and gives it a default title. With an mcml heatmap or index view, a value other than "both" raises an error.

expand

For an mcml: the clusters whose member states are shown individually in the Summary panel; "all" or TRUE expands every cluster. The per-cluster panels are unaffected. Default NULL keys the Summary panel by cluster.

combine

For an mcml: clusters to merge into one channel. A character vector merges one group (e.g. combine = c("Cognitive", "Affective")); a list merges several, and its names label the merged channels (default label "Cognitive + Affective"). A merged group acts as one cluster throughout the figure: one per-cluster panel holding all its states, one key in the Summary panel, and one faded band in the other panels. expand is resolved after merging, so it can name the merged label. An unknown cluster, a group of fewer than two, or a cluster in two groups raises an error. Default NULL draws the partition as built.

rest

For an mcml: how a cluster's panel shows the time its subjects spend in other clusters. "clusters" (default) draws one faded band (or wash, in the carpet) per other cluster; "pooled" draws all other clusters as one grey band labelled rest_label; "none" leaves them blank, so the panel shows only its own states. In the distribution view "none" drops the NA (ended) band too, and the panel's height at each time point is the share of subjects in that cluster. Ignored with normalize = TRUE, which rescales each panel to its own states. The Summary panel is unaffected.

rest_label

For an mcml: the legend text for time spent in other clusters. Default "Other states"; "Others" or "Rest of states" are alternatives. The pooled band (rest = "pooled") takes it as is; the per-cluster bands read "Social (Other states)". A label equal to a state or cluster name, or to "NA", raises an error. combine, expand, rest and rest_label on any input other than an mcml raise an error.

trim_clusterwise

For a grouped index or distribution view with a fractional trim: FALSE (default) computes one cut on the pooled data and applies it to every panel, so all panels share the same width and the time axes stay aligned; TRUE judges the time points within each group, so panels can end up at different widths. An absolute trim (>= 1) ignores it, since the cut is the same everywhere.

row_gap

The vertical gap between rows of the index view, as a fraction of the row height, in [0, 1). Default 0 (dense, like the heatmap); 0.15 gives visible separators when there are few rows.

dendrogram_width

The width of the heatmap's dendrogram panel, against a carpet width of 4: the default 1.2 makes the dendrogram 0.3 times as wide as the carpet. Used only when a dendrogram is drawn.

k

For the heatmap: the number of clusters to cut the dendrogram into, a single number of at least 2 and less than the number of rows; thin horizontal lines then separate them in the carpet. Ignored without a dendrogram (e.g. sort = "start") and in the other views. Default NULL (no separators).

k_color

The colour of the cluster separator lines. Default "white".

k_line_width

The line width of the cluster separators. Default 2.5.

state_colors

Colours for the fill keys, in one of two forms: unnamed, one colour per state in level order (states are ordered as sort(unique(...))); or named, a lookup where only the keys you name are overridden and every other key keeps its default (Okabe-Ito). Names this figure does not draw are dropped with a message naming them, so one project-wide palette can be handed to every plot and each takes the keys that apply to it. Default NULL uses the palette attached to x with set_state_colors(), if any; a palette given here wins for this figure.

For an mcml the named form reaches the whole figure, not only the states: a cluster name colours its Summary band, its channel strip and its faded band in the other panels, and a group merged by combine is named by its label (the list name you gave it, or "A + B"). rest_label is a key too. So state_colors = c(plan = "#0072B2", "Planning + Monitoring" = "#D55E00") recolours one state and one combined cluster and leaves the rest of the palette alone.

na_color

The colour of missing cells. Default "grey90"; with periods, "white" unless given.

cell_border

The colour of each cell's border. Default NA (no border).

frame

Whether to draw a box around each panel; axis ticks and labels appear either way. Default FALSE.

width, height

Device dimensions in inches. In an interactive session, giving either opens a new graphics device with grDevices::dev.new() (the other defaults to 7); otherwise they are ignored. In knitr chunks, use the fig.width and fig.height chunk options instead. Default NULL.

main

The plot title. Default NULL: no title, apart from "n = N" when show_n = TRUE. With several groups, main is drawn once above the panels, and not at all when combined = FALSE.

show_n

Whether to append "(n = N)" to the title (to each panel title when grouped). Default TRUE.

time_label, xlab

The x-axis label; xlab is an alias that wins when given. Default "Time" (with periods, the period column's name).

y_label, ylab

The y-axis label of the distribution view; ylab is an alias. Default NULL, which distribution_plot() reads as "Proportion" or "Count" according to scale.

tick

Label every tick-th time point on the x-axis. Default NULL thins the labels to about 15.

ncol, nrow

The panel grid of the grouped index and distribution views. Default NULL: with neither given, ncol = ceiling(sqrt(G)) for G groups and nrow = ceiling(G / ncol); with one given, the other follows. With combined = FALSE the grid does not affect the layout, but ncol * nrow must still be at least the number of groups or an error is raised.

combined

For the grouped index and distribution views: TRUE (default) arranges the groups on one figure with graphics::layout(); FALSE draws each group on its own page, at full size with its own legend. A single group ignores it, and the heatmap is always one figure.

legend

The legend position: "right", "bottom" or "none". Default NULL, read as "right" for every view.

legend_size

The legend text size. Default NULL scales it with the device width so the legend stays in proportion on a 5-inch and a 12-inch figure (between 0.65 and 1.2).

legend_title

The legend title. Default NULL (none).

legend_ncol

The number of legend columns. Default NULL: one row for a bottom legend, one column for a right legend.

legend_border

The colour of the legend swatches' borders. Default NA (none).

legend_bty

The legend box: "n" (default, none) or "o" (boxed).

cols

For a wide data frame: the columns holding the positions. Needed when they are not a numbered run (T1, T2, ...), when one of them is called action, or when any other column sits beside them; given for any other input it raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input, except for an mcml, which ignores it. Default NULL.

...

For the print() method: ignored.

Value

For an mcml: the multichannel figure, one panel per channel (the macro Summary and one per cluster), stacked, each with its own legend of its clusters or states. When more than one channel is drawn it is an mcml_sequence_plot, a gtable that its print() method draws on a new page; when panel = "summary" leaves a single channel it is a ggplot. The print() method returns its input invisibly.

Every other input is drawn with base graphics, and the call returns, invisibly, a list describing the figure, whose fields depend on the view:

heatmap

ord (the row order plotted, as integer indices), codes (the integer-coded, trimmed sequence matrix), palette, levels (the state labels, parallel to palette) and sort_used (the ordering applied; "net_clustering" when a clustering's dendrogram was used).

index

codes, palette, levels, orders (a list of row orders, one per panel, indexing the original rows) and groups (the panel labels).

with periods

ord (the row order of the actors), codes (an integer matrix, one row per actor and one column per period slot in the fill = "pad" layout, named "<period>.<slot>"), palette, levels, periods (the period labels in plotted order, after trim) and fill; with group, also groups (the panel labels) and orders (one row order per panel, indexing the actors), ord being their concatenation.

distribution

What distribution_plot() returns: counts, proportions, levels, palette and groups.

Multichannel view of an mcml

An mcml built from sequences stores, for every cluster, the full sequence matrix with the other clusters' states blanked out. Each cluster is therefore a channel, and sequence_plot() stacks them:

Summary

The macro sequence: at every time point, the cluster each subject is in.

One panel per cluster

That cluster's own states, plus the time its subjects spend in the other clusters.

The options apply in this order, so each one sees the result of the one before:

  1. combine merges clusters into one channel. The merged group is then one cluster throughout the figure: one panel with all its states, one Summary key, one band in the other panels. The object itself is not changed.

  2. expand opens clusters (including a merged group, by its label) into their member states in the Summary panel only.

  3. rest and rest_label set how a cluster's panel shows the other clusters: one faded band per cluster labelled "<cluster> (<rest_label>)" (rest = "clusters"), one grey band labelled rest_label ("pooled"), or nothing ("none").

  4. na (distribution only) keeps the NA band of sequences that have ended (TRUE, shares of all subjects) or drops it (FALSE, shares of the subjects still running, so every panel stacks to 100 percent unless rest = "none"). normalize = TRUE instead rescales each cluster panel to its own states, which ignores rest and na.

panel draws the Summary or the cluster panels alone, and trim cuts the time axis for every panel at once.

Methods

  • print.mcml_sequence_plot() draws the figure sequence_plot() returns for an mcml with more than one channel (the macro Summary and one panel per cluster, each with its own legend) on a new page of the current graphics device.

See also

distribution_plot, build_clusters, build_mcml

Examples

sequence_plot(trajectories)


# \donttest{
sequence_plot(trajectories, type = "index")

sequence_plot(trajectories, type = "distribution")


# One row per student, one block per day; each day's actions fill it.
daily <- data.frame(
  student = rep(c("s1", "s2", "s3"), times = c(5, 9, 6)),
  day     = c("d1", "d2", "d2", "d3", "d3",
              "d1", "d1", "d2", "d2", "d2", "d3", "d3", "d3", "d3",
              "d1", "d1", "d1", "d2", "d3", "d3"),
  action  = c("plan", "read", "write", "read", "plan",
              "read", "read", "plan", "write", "write", "read", "plan",
              "write", "read", "plan", "plan", "write", "read", "write",
              "read"))
sequence_plot(daily, actor = "student", action = "action", periods = "day")

sequence_plot(daily, actor = "student", action = "action", periods = "day",
              fill = "pad", type = "index")


# The same from a network built with the period as its session.
daily_net <- build_network(daily, method = "relative", actor = "student",
                           action = "action", session = "day")
sequence_plot(daily_net, periods = "day")


# Multichannel MCML view: one channel per cluster + a macro Summary.
fit <- build_mcml(
  group_regulation_long,
  clusters = list(Cognitive  = c("discuss", "synthesis", "consensus", "cohesion"),
                  Regulation = c("plan", "monitor", "adapt", "coregulate"),
                  Affective  = "emotion"),
  actor = "Actor", action = "Action", time = "Time")
sequence_plot(fit)                                          # multichannel carpet


# Shape the multichannel view (see the section above).
sequence_plot(fit, type = "distribution",
              combine = list(Task = c("Cognitive", "Regulation")),
              expand = "Task")                              # merge, then open


# Colour by name: one state, one cluster, one combined group. Everything
# not named keeps its default colour.
sequence_plot(fit, type = "distribution",
              combine = list(Task = c("Cognitive", "Regulation")),
              state_colors = c(Task = "#0072B2", Affective = "#D55E00",
                               emotion = "#CC79A7"))

# }
